terms.gloss: put heads together, confer in secret
terms.grammar: cōnferō with capita, plural of caput
evidence: Liv. 2.45.7: cōnsulēs velut dēlīberābundī capita cōnferunt, diū colloquuntur (Lewis & Short s.v. dēlīberābundus)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. caput: “like our phrase to put heads together, i.e. to confer together in secret”.

sources: Lewis & Short: caput · Lewis & Short: confero
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 100, 326.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
